messages.content: I am interested in purchasing a house. I decided to consult a certain agent. I went to their office and discussed my needs. The agent told me that there is a house on the market that is an excellent fit for me needs, and that I should tour and purchase the house very soon as there are many interested buyers on the market. I learned that many real estate agents earn commissions from house sales (that is, they earn some percent of the total sale price). Moreover, the size of this commission varies from house to house. I also learned that there are other houses on the market.

Say that the agent I am talking with is my agent friend, and they will receive 10% of the sale price as commission from selling me this home. On a scale from 0 to 100, rate how beneficial you think this bonus would be for my agent friend, with 0 meaning getting this bonus would not matter at all and 100 meaning would be extremely good to get this bonus, based on how my agent friend would likely perceive its value. Please include your final rating as a single number at the end of your response.

A 10% commission on a house sale is significantly higher than the typical real estate commission (often in the neighborhood of 2–3%). Because commissions can be a major source of income, this extra-high percentage would likely feel like an exceptionally beneficial windfall from the agent’s perspective, especially if the house is reasonably high-priced. Factoring in the potential to earn a sizable amount in one transaction, I would consider it extremely valuable, landing near the upper end of the scale.
